title: EU AI Act (amended) pack 2026.10.1 - three sample requirements
notes: Draft fixture for design issue #26. Source: templates/catalog.json and docs/obligation-subitems.json at commit 74c6463. Items WP-A09-01, WP-XC-01 and WP-XC-07 are copied verbatim; requirements Art. 9 (with 9(1)), Art. 17 and Art. 50, plus Art. 16 because WP-XC-01 cites it. Not a release. The index shows how the two documents are listed once released under Q4 option (b): the methodology owner releases the framework while its qualified legal review is pending, and the legal reviewer's approval is appended later. The digests are the real JCS digests of the two documents; names and dates are example values.

documents.notes: Design sample for issue #26: the subset of the framework needed by three catalogue items. Article nodes come from the catalogue regulatoryRefs; child requirements from docs/obligation-subitems.json; requirement-level application dates are not recorded in data version 2026.10.1 (see applicationSummary). compat.obligations keeps the obligation file's top-level fields verbatim and its item order, restricted to the sample's one subitem.

obligations.scope: Selective audit prompts for Articles 9-15, Annex IV and associated actor duties; grouped references are explicit and this is not an exhaustive EU AI Act catalog.

applicationContext.covers: Chapter III Sections 1, 2 and 3 except Article 6(5)
applicationContext.approvalRule: Dates inform review; they do not automatically approve applicability. Assess Articles 2 and 111, route, actor, intended use, relevant modifications and sectoral rules. Annex I Section B requires sectoral-route analysis under Article 2(2), rather than automatic direct Section 2 application.
applicationContext.sourceCurrencyRule: Source publication, research and application dates have different meanings. A new source version creates an impact-review candidate and never rewrites a historical decision.

decisionPolicy.providerResponsibility: Articles 9-15 are system requirements; provider responsibility is linked through Article 16(a). A deployer may inspect provider evidence but does not thereby assume every provider duty. Article 25 role changes need separate review.
decisionPolicy.dataScope: Under Article 10(1), datasets used for data-trained models are assessed; Article 10(6) limits Article 10(2)-(4) and Article 4a(1) to testing datasets for systems without model training. Article 10(5) was deleted; special-category processing is a separate Article 4a/data-protection assessment, not an upload permission.
decisionPolicy.retention: Retention is actor, control, purpose and law dependent. Article 26(6) is not one universal evidence-vault retention policy.
decisionPolicy.excludedActorDuties: Other provider, deployer, representative, importer, distributor, sectoral, conformity, registration and fundamental-rights duties must be added where applicable. This selective catalog does not waive them.

triggerType.evaluation: Candidate selection only. Unknown in a required predicate yields needs_information. Legal-period approval and scope exclusions are separate human decisions.

items.title: Lifecycle risk management system
items.objective: Assess documented lifecycle identification, treatment and reassessment of risks.

procedures.text: Trace sampled risks through identification, mitigation, testing and residual-risk acceptance.
Challenge misuse, vulnerable-group harms, interactions and completeness with domain specialists.
Reconcile material risks to predefined metrics, thresholds and versioned validation evidence.
Inspect monitoring/incident-driven risk updates and accountability.

items.signOffGate: Independent reviewer clears blocking notes and approves the exact revision; lead approval where material.

items.title: Quality management and governance
items.objective: Assess relevant accountable governance and quality management processes.

procedures.text: Inspect documented responsibilities, approvals, design/change controls and quality processes.
Sample control operation, supplier management, training and escalations.
Reconcile governance procedures to actual product releases and risk decisions.

items.signOffGate: Independent reviewer clears blocking notes and approves the exact revision; lead approval where material.

items.objective: Assess applicable transparency duties separately from high-risk routing.

procedures.text: Assess provider/deployer and use-based transparency applicability and transitions.
Inspect notices, content labeling/detection solutions or other required measures within scope.
Observe user-facing behavior and approved exceptions with legal rationale.
